name: Factions
descr:
Factions let you group characters into named in-game organizations: nations, guilds, classes, or secret societies. This tutorial covers the three faction types and explains how they affect the character gallery and character sheets.

Manage factions

To group the characters in factions, activate the Factions feature.

In Event > Factions, click on "New" to create a new faction:

Type: There are three: Primary (Used for main grouping in the gallery, such as nation, core affiliation), Transversal (Cross-grouping across primary faction, such as class, race, profession), Secret (Hidden faction, visible only to assigned characters, used for secret plots)

  • Name: Public name of the faction
  • Presentation: Public description of the faction
  • Text: Private description, visible only to participants in the faction
  • Characters: List of characters assigned to this faction

A character can be assigned to only one "Primary" faction.

In the character gallery, characters are grouped under their primary faction:

To show the factions to participants, toggle the visibility in Event > Event:

If the Character creation feature is active (see the Character Creation tutorial), a new checkbox, Selectable, is added to the faction form.

Participants can select this faction in the Faction field when creating or editing their character.

Related tutorials: Characters, Guilds, Casting

name: Plots
descr:
Plots are storylines that involve several characters: each plot has a shared text, and a personal role for every character in it. This tutorial explains how to create plots, assign characters to them, and what participants see.

Creating plots

To manage storylines that span across multiple characters, enable the Plots feature.

Then, in Event > Plots, click on "New" to create a new one:

  • Name: name of the plot, visible to the characters involved.
  • Concept: internal notes for the staff, not visible to participants.
  • Text: the shared storyline, shown to all the characters involved.
  • Characters: the characters taking part in the storyline. When you add a character, a new row appears where you write the personal role of that character:

Roles in the character form

You can also edit the role of a character in a plot from the character edit page:

Participant view

Once the character is assigned to a participant, the text of each plot and the personal role are shown in the character page:

Plot list and statistics

Event > Plots lists all the plots of the event. Use the buttons above the table to show more columns, such as the characters involved and their number.

In Event > Configuration > Characters, enable Unimportant to mark minor roles: start the personal role text with $unimportant, and a new column counts only the important characters of each plot. The marker is never shown to participants.

Custom fields and tracking

You can add custom fields to plots in Event > Sheet, as for characters (see Character Sheet). There you can also add the Progress and Assigned fields, to track the writing status of each plot and the staff member responsible for it.

Visibility

Plots are shown to a participant only once a character is assigned to them. If you control which elements participants can see, select Plots among the elements shown in Event > Event (see Characters).

To read all the plots and characters of the event in one place, use Event > Reading.

Related tutorials: Characters, Factions, Writing Extras

name: Quests and Traits
descr:
Quests and traits let you write parts of character sheets as reusable pieces, which participants can choose and which are then assigned to characters. This tutorial explains the three concepts, how to create them, and how they are assigned.

Key concepts

To use them, activate the Quests and Traits feature. There are three key concepts:

  • Trait: a single text element assigned to a character. Each trait belongs to a quest (e.g., roles in a heist: Mind, Muscle, Face).
  • Quest: a collection of traits sharing a common theme (e.g., Heist). Each quest belongs to a quest type.
  • Quest type: a grouping of quests within the same category (e.g., Past Occupations).

Each character can have at most one trait for each quest type.

Creating quest types, quests and traits

To create a quest type, go to Event > Quest type and click "New":

To create a quest, go to Event > Quest and click "New":

  • Type: the quest type;
  • Name: name of the quest;
  • Presentation: shown to all participants;
  • Text: visible only to characters assigned a trait of this quest.

To create a trait, go to Event > Traits and click "New":

  • Quest: the quest of the trait;
  • Name: name of the trait;
  • Presentation: shown to all participants;
  • Text: visible only to characters assigned this trait.

Referencing other traits

When writing a trait, you can reference other traits with their number, in the format #<Number>. Once the traits are assigned, the reference is replaced with the name of the character who received that trait.

For example, if the Muscle trait has number 2, writing #2 in the Mind trait shows the participant with the Mind trait the name of the character with the Muscle trait.

Participant view

Participants find a new entry, Quest, in the event menu, listing the quests:

Clicking a quest shows its presentation and traits:

Assigning traits

If the Casting algorithm feature is active (see the Casting tutorial), participants choose the traits they prefer for each quest type:

You then assign them in Event > Casting, selecting the quest type at the top:

You can also assign a trait directly when editing a registration in Event > Registrations:

Related tutorials: Casting, Characters

name: Deadlines
descr:
The Deadlines feature helps you track participants who have missed key milestones, such as completing registration, submitting their character, or paying, and send them automated reminders. This tutorial covers how to configure tolerances and review the missed deadlines.

Deadlines

To monitor participants who have missed a deadline regarding their registration, activate the Deadlines feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Deadline, you find two options:

  • Tolerance: In Event > Deadlines, all registrations that missed a deadline are listed. Those exceeding the defined tolerance (in days) appear in a separate row. Registrations are not deleted automatically; removal must be done manually.
  • Frequency: Email alerts are sent every specified number of days per event to users with the "Organizer" role.

For each event you find Event > Deadlines, that summarizes all missed deadlines:

The monitored deadlines include: Payment deadlines (full amount, dynamic rates, or fixed installments), Completion of personal data in the user profile
If the Membership feature is active, checks also cover: Submission of the membership registration request, Payment of the annual membership fee

Reminders

To send automatic reminders to participants for their deadlines, activate the Reminder feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Reminder, you find two options:

Reminder emails are sent for the previously outlined deadlines.

It is also possible to customize the text of the emails in Organization > Texts:

Related tutorials: Membership, Mail Settings, Registrations

name: Mail Settings
descr:
The platform sends automated emails to participants at key moments: registration confirmation, payment received, character assigned, and more. This tutorial explains how to customize those templates, configure a custom mail server, and manage mail-related settings.

Mail notifications

You can configure the emails that LarpManager sends when participants act. Go to Organization > Configuration > Email notifications:

Notifications digest

Receive a single daily summary instead of one email for each new registration, update, payment or invoice to approve.

For the main email address of the organization, enable Notifications digest in Organization > Configuration > Email notifications (the option is shown only if the organization has a main email address).

Each organizer can also choose it for their own notifications, in Organization > Preferences:

Notifications are then collected during the day and sent together in one summary email.

Custom mail server

By default, LarpManager sends emails from <slug>@larpmanager.com using its own mail servers. This feature allows configuring an external mail server by providing its connection details. First, activate the External mail server feature.

Set the mail server details in Organization > Configuration > Customised mail server:

Insert the required information; all the emails regarding your events are sent using those connection details.

If you're not sure, ask your email provider for these details.

If you encounter any issue, please contact us, or your email provider, to check them.

You can configure a mail server individually for each event. If an event has a custom mail server setting, those are used instead of the ones of the whole organization.

To override it for a single event, use Event > Configuration > Customised mail server, with the same required information.

Related tutorials: Deadlines, Organization Appearance

name: Ensemble
descr:
This tutorial presents Ensemble, a tool that helps players learn all the characters of the event before it starts, with printable cards, a booklet and a mobile-friendly list.

What is Ensemble?

Ensemble facilitates an accessible presentation of characters and a quick way to learn them. It provides organizers and players with a very flexible tool and intuitive interface for presenting, sorting and categorizing characters. Remembering them is made easy, social and fun through a deck of flash cards, a booklet as well as an online database. There is no need for layout skills, Ensemble lets you print the cards and booklet with all layout done, and you don't need an app to access the characters from your phone.

Ensemble is suitable for all kinds of larps, from small chamber larps where the organizer presents the players with pre-written characters and fixed relations, up to and including huge sandbox games where the players write their characters and group affiliations themselves.

Why Ensemble?

So many of the larps we play portray very close-knit communities, be it a village, a spaceship, a military unit, a prison camp or a school class. You will typically have close relationships with a few other characters, and maybe learn about a couple more, but the feeling that you really ought to know all of them intimately lingers.

Through Ensemble the players can realistically be expected to arrive at the site already knowing most of the other characters. This means less onsite time has to be allocated for character and group presentation workshops. Players will be more familiar with the social structure of the larp and feel less stress about "who is who", they will feel more immersed and can more easily play with everyone instead of just the players they know the best. Basically, the players will have a better game.

How to use

Once you activate the Ensemble feature, the user interface will show the link to the dedicated page:

In it, there are three views available: Book (to show all the characters in a booklet format), Cards (to show / print the characters in the cards format), Compact list (to show the characters in list format).

Once the feature is active, in the Factions edit page it will be possible to choose a color; the card of a character will show at the top the colors of the factions assigned.

(Many thanks to Janusz Maxe and Lars Nordbeck for sharing their work!)

Related tutorials: Characters, Factions

name: Accounting
descr:
The platform tracks the financial side of every registration automatically. This tutorial covers the accounting views available to participants (personal balance and registration fees) and to organizers (global balance, per-event breakdown, and individual accounting management).

User accounting

Each user can access their personal accounting from the "Accounting" entry of the user menu.

This page summarizes any pending payments, if present, and the accounting status of all their registrations.

Organization accounting

To view an overview of the organization's accounting, go to Organization > Accounting.

At the top, you'll see the Global Balance. This reflects the organization's positive operating margin, based solely on the budgets of events marked as "Completed."

If Tokens or Credits are enabled, this balance assumes that all of them have already been used or refunded.

This is a virtual balance, indicating the available margin for planning organizational expenses.

Below that is the Overall Balance. This represents the actual amount that should be held across the organization's bank and financial accounts. To align this with your real financial status when you start using LarpManager, record an Inflow (see below) with the current amount held.

Note: Additional summary rows will appear if you activate more Accounting features.

Event accounting

To view an overview of an event's accounting, go to Event > Accounting.

This overview allows you to monitor actual versus expected income, track payment methods, and calculate net event profitability.

Below you find a breakdown of each accounting type.

Donation

To allow users to perform voluntary donations to the organization, activate the Donation feature.

Users can now find a Donate section on their accounting page.

Following their link they can perform the donation, that is recorded as an organization inflow.

Tokens

To use tokens, activate the Tokens feature. Each user will have an associated token balance. The primary function of tokens is to automatically reduce the registration fee when a user signs up for an event - one token per unit of the organization's configured currency (e.g., 1 token per €1).

LarpManager handles token accounting automatically. This allows the organization to reward participants or collaborators by granting tokens, which they can then use to lower the cost of future event registrations.

To issue tokens to a user, you can add them from Event > Tokens (in which case they are counted as event expenses) or from Organization > Tokens (in which case they are counted as organizational expenses).

You can also customize the display names in Organization > Configuration > Tokens; the list with the total amounts of tokens for all users is available in Organization > Accounting.

Credits

To use credits, activate the Credits feature. They function similarly to tokens but with a key difference: they represent a real debt the organization owes to the user. Unlike tokens, credits can either be used to reduce event registration fees or be refunded upon request (see below: Refunds).

They can also be used to reimburse collaborators who have incurred expenses while organizing events (see below: Expenses).

To issue credits to a user, you can add them from Event > Credits (in which case they are counted as event expenses) or from Organization > Credits (in which case they are counted as organizational expenses).

You can also customize the display names used in Organization > Configuration > Credits; the list with the total amounts of credits for all users is available in Organization > Accounting.

Expenses

To allow collaborators to upload receipts for event-related expenses and receive reimbursement in Credits, enable the Expenses feature.

Each staff member can upload these receipts from Event > Upload Expenses by clicking on "New":

Expenses can then be reviewed in Event > Expenses, or globally in Organization > Expenses:

Once approved, an equal amount of Credits is issued to the user.

Collections

To allow users to start pooled collections to give a gift to another user, enable the Collections feature.

Users can now find a Collection section on their accounting page:

When a collection is created, a shareable link is provided for inviting other friends to contribute:

When a collection is closed, the amount can be issued as Credits to the recipient from Organization > Collections.

Refunds

To allow users to request a refund for accumulated Credits, enable the Refunds feature.

Users can now find a Refund section on their accounting page:

You can then review the requests in the Organization's Refunds page:

After completing the payout, click "Done" to mark the refund as reimbursed.

Inflows

To manage inflows of money beyond participant registration fees, enable the Inflows feature.

Inflows can be added either in Event > Inflows, or in Organization > Inflows:

Outflows

To manage outflows of money paid through the organization's financial accounts, enable the Outflows feature.

Outflows can be added either in Event > Outflows, or in Organization > Outflows:

Taxes

To automatically calculate taxes due on received payments, activate the Taxes feature.

Set the taxes percentage in Organization > Configuration > VAT:

The taxes due amount is displayed in Organization > Payments:

Verification payments

In the payment processing system, bank transfers are manually approved by organizers. As an additional verification measure to confirm the arrival of funds, enable the Verification payments feature.

Now Organization > Verification displays all received bank transfers that have not yet been verified:

You can upload a CSV file to verify payments in bulk. This payment list can be obtained from your bank or equivalent provider; it must have the payment amount as the first column and the bank transfer reference as the second.

(The unique code automatically added by LarpManager to outgoing payments helps identify them during this verification phase)

Organization tax

To automatically set aside a portion of an event's revenue as organizational self-funding, enable the Organizational fee feature.

Set the organization tax percentage in Organization > Configuration > Organizational fee:

In Event > Accounting, a new entry is added for the organization tax calculated amount:

Treasurer

Send payment confirmations to your treasurers, instead of to the organizers of each event. To use it, activate the Treasurer feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Treasury, select the users in Appointees; they receive the payment confirmation emails for all events.

Accounting tracking

Keep a daily history of your finances. To use it, activate the Accounting tracking feature.

Every day, LarpManager records the financial status of the organization and of each event. The trend graphs are shown in Organization > Historical.

Related tutorials: Payments, Registration Accounting, Italian Associations

name: Users
descr:
This tutorial covers the features for managing participants and users. It explains how to handle in-platform help requests from participants, give the safety and diet teams access to sensitive participant data, enable private messaging between users, manage your newsletter contacts, and allow users to create and operate delegated accounts on behalf of others.

Help

To manage participant help requests directly in the platform, activate the Help feature.

Participants will now see a "Need help?" link at the bottom of every page in the interface.

Clicking on "Need help" will open a new page:

Below they will also see the full list of messages and replies from the staff:

To answer, you can use either Event > Questions for each event, or Organization > Questions for all of them:

You can aswer them, or close them if no further actions are needed.

Safety

If you have selected the "Safety" field in Organization > Profile (see Organization profile in the Personal Data tutorial), a new page Event > Safety is available for each event:

This page can then be shared only with the safety team, so that only they can access this sensitive information.

Diet

If you have selected the "Diet" field in Organization > Profile (see Organization profile in the Personal Data tutorial), a new page Event > Diet is available for each event:

This page can then be shared only with the food team, so that only they can access this sensitive information.

Chat

To allow users to safely message each other through the platform, activate the Chat feature.

In each user profile (reachable clicking of the user in the event gallery), a new link is available:

Clicking on it, another user can send a private message.

Note: the messages are directly sent to the user's emails, without exposing them to the other user.

Neswletter

To manage the list of emails of users that have given permission to share their data with your organization, activate the Newsletter feature.

In Organization > Newsletter, you find them, categorized by the preference they have expressed, and their language:

Note: please respect the user's newsletter subscription preferences when sending messages.

Delegated users

To allow users to manage delegated accounts (for example for friends or for children), activate the Delegated accounts feature.

Users will now see a new option, "Delegated users", in the user menu.

Going in that link will show a page to manage delegated users:

They can now create new delegated users; or clicking on "Login", to access the platform with that account, performing registrations, o

Note: delegated users may later be upgraded to stand-alone users by submitting a request to the platform administrators.

Badges

Award badges to users, and show them in a public leaderboard. To use it, activate the Badge feature.

Go to Organization > Badges and click "New":

  • Name: short name of the badge (with its international version).
  • Description: what the badge rewards (with its international version).
  • Code: internal code, without spaces or symbols.
  • Img: the badge image.

Assign the badge to users from its edit page. Users see their badges in their profile, and everyone can see the leaderboard.

Vote

Let members elect the executive committee of your organization online. To use it, activate the Vote feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Voting, set:

  • Active: if checked, members can vote.
  • Candidates: the users standing for election.
  • Minimum votes: the minimum number of candidates each member must choose.
  • Maximum votes: the maximum number of candidates each member can choose.

While voting is active, members find a link to the vote page in their profile. The results are shown in Organization > Vote.

Related tutorials: User Flags, Personal Data, Membership

name: Membership
descr:
The Membership feature implements a formal onboarding process for your organization's members. Only approved members can pay and participate in the organization's event. New participants are prompted to download a membership request document pre-filled with their data, sign it, and upload the signed copy for staff approval.

You can also require payment of an annual membership fee, and track the status of every member directly from the registrations of each event.

Membership

To implement a formal approval process for members registering for an event, activate the Membership feature.

Set the values in Organization > Configuration > Members:

  • Age: Minimum age required for individuals to be eligible as members (can be blank).
  • Annual Fee: The yearly membership fee that each member must pay, calculated from the start of the membership year (can be left empty if not present). Participating in any event in a membership year requires the payment of the membership fee; if not paid, it is added to the first payment of event registration for that year.
  • Start Day: The calendar day on which the membership year officially begins. Format: DD-MM (e.g., 01-01 for January 1st).
  • Standalone Payment Window: Normally users are able to pay the membership fee only if they are signed up for an event in the current membership year. If you wish to allow them a window of time where they can pay the membership fee anyway, set the value here (can be blank).

Membership request template

You need to set up the membership document template text. Go to Organization > Texts, and you find a new text type:

Define the template for the membership request document in this field. An example could be:

I, the undersigned {{ member.surname }} {{ member.name }}, born on {{ member.birth_date }} in {{ member.birth_place }}, residing at {{ member.get_residence }}, holding {{ member.get_document_type_display }} no. {{ member.document }}, phone {{ member.phone_contact }}, email {{ member.user.email }}, hereby request the Board of Directors to be admitted as a member of the Association.

When an user signs up for their first event of the Organization, the request document will automatically populated with the user's data. Users will then download the PDF document, only sign it, and upload the signed copy.

After a confirmation page, the request is then sent to the Board.

To review members, go to Organization > Members. The new requests are at the top of the list:

Clicking on "Request", you open a page where you can either Approve the request, and the user is accepted as new member. At the bottom, you can also Reject it (if for example the documentation is not correct). The user will then be able to submit a new request.

Membership fee

If you've selected a value for the yearly membership fee, each participant of event in the current year is prompted to pay it.

In Organization > Members you can review the users that have already paid it, or you can approve the payments done by wire / freeform.

You can also upload the membership documents for a member, or the receipt of the payment of their membership fee, with the "Upload membership document" and "Upload membership fee" buttons at the top of the list.

In Event > Registrations of each event, you'll also find a column with the membership status:

The values are:

  • Inactive (E): no membership data yet;
  • Inactive (J): the user has agreed to share their data, but has not uploaded a membership request (first step);
  • Inactive (U): the user has uploaded the request, but has not confirmed it (second step);
  • Review: the user has confirmed the request, which is waiting for your approval (third step);
  • Accepted: the user is a member;
  • Removed: the member status has been revoked.

Membership deadlines

If you have also activated the Deadlines feature, in Organization > Deadlines you find a recap on the users that have not yet submitted the membership request (or paid the annual membership fee, if a values has been set):

Additional texts

In Organization > Texts, three more text types become available when Membership is active:

  • Association Statute: Optional text shown at the bottom of the membership page, to already-accepted members. Use it to display the association statute or any information relevant to full members.
  • Membership request reminder email: Body of the automated reminder email sent to registered participants who have not yet completed their membership request. If left blank, a built-in default message is used, which includes a direct link to the membership application page.
  • Membership fee reminder email: Body of the automated reminder email sent to registered participants who have not yet paid the annual membership fee. If left blank, a built-in default message is used, which includes a link to the payment page and a note about the insurance requirement.

Note: the reminder emails are sent automatically by the daily automation task. To configure when they are triggered, see the Deadlines tutorial.

Member detail

From Organization > Members, clicking on a member's name opens their detail page. From there you can access two sub-sections:

  • Registrations: List of all event registrations for that member within the association, with costs and payment status.
  • Accounting: Full payment and accounting history for that member within the association (payments, tokens, credits, discounts).
  • Membership: Membership status, uploaded request and document, card number and newsletter preference.

Membership registry

Organization > Registry lists all accepted members who have been assigned a card number, ordered by card number. It is designed to serve as the official membership register of the association.

To access it, you need the Registry permission enabled in Organization > Roles.

Enrollment list

Organization > Insurance Data shows the list of members who have paid the annual membership fee for the current year, together with their card number and enrollment date. This list is useful if you have an insurance based on the yearly payment of the membership fee.

To access it, you need the Insurance Data permission enabled in Organization > Roles.

Related tutorials: Users, User Flags, Deadlines, Payments

name: Check-in
descr:
This tutorial explains how to use Check-in to mark participants as present on-site by scanning their QR code, even without an internet connection. Use it whenever you need a fast, paperless accreditation desk at your event.

Activating check-in

To use it, activate the Check-in feature.

A new page, Event > Check-in, becomes available in the event dashboard.

Note: to let other staff members use it, assign them the Check-in permission in Event > Roles.

Participant QR code

Once the feature is active, every participant receives a personal QR code, linked to their registration:

  • It is shown on the event page, next to their registration status.
  • It is attached as an image to the registration confirmation email (and to the update emails).

Ask participants to bring the code on their phone or printed. The code does not change if the registration is edited.

Check-in page

Go to Event > Check-in.

The page lists all active registrations of the event (cancelled registrations and pending registration requests are excluded), with these columns:

  • Participant: name of the participant.
  • Character: assigned characters (with their number, if character numbers are enabled).
  • Payment: "Paid" if the registration fee is fully paid, otherwise "Outstanding".
  • Present: whether the participant has already been checked in.

Use the search box to filter the list by participant or character name.

Click the info icon at the start of a row to open the participant details: ticket, faction, answers to the registration form, and the fields of their character sheet.

At the bottom of the page, a summary shows the number of participants Present, Not scanned, and the Total.

Note: the payment status is shown for information only; it does not prevent the check-in.

Scanning a QR code

Click on Scan QR code, and allow the browser to use the camera. Point the camera at the participant's QR code.

When the code is recognized, the participant is immediately marked as present, and the popup shows "Checked in:" followed by their name. You can keep scanning other codes without closing the popup.

  • If the code does not belong to this event, the message "Unknown QR code for this event." is shown.
  • If a participant is scanned twice, the time of the first check-in is kept.

Manual check-in

If a participant cannot show their QR code (lost phone, no battery), find them with the search box in Event > Check-in, then click Sign in on their row, and confirm.

Offline mode

The whole participant list is downloaded when the page is opened, so the page keeps working if the device loses connectivity (common at outdoor or remote venues).

At the top of the page, an indicator shows whether you are Online or Offline. While offline, scans and manual check-ins are applied to the list immediately and saved in the browser; the counter Pending sync shows how many are waiting to be sent.

As soon as the connection is restored, pending check-ins are sent automatically, keeping their original scan time.

Note: open the page while you still have a connection, and use the same device and browser until all pending check-ins are synced. Do not clear the browser data before that.

Experience points for attendance

This requires the Experience points feature to also be active (see the Experience Points tutorial).

To give experience points only to the characters of participants that actually attended, go to Event > Awards, open the Load characters menu and select From checked-in participants.

The new award form is pre-filled with the characters of all checked-in participants; set the amount of points and save.

Related tutorials: Registrations, Experience Points, Event Tools

name: Casting
descr:
The Casting feature lets participants express preferences for which characters they would like to play, then runs an algorithm to assign characters automatically based on those preferences. This tutorial covers setup, the participant preference flow, and how to run and review the assignment.

Casting algorithm

To manage participant preferences on characters and perform assignment with an algorithm, activate the Casting algorithm feature.

In Event > Configuration > Casting, set those values:

When a participant is signed up and has fewer assigned characters than the Assignments value, an additional navigation bar button will appear, allowing them to request or select more characters.

For each preference, the participant first selects a faction on the left, then a character on the right.

Once the number of preferences entered is between the defined Minimum Preferences and Maximum Preferences, they can be submitted.

Participants may update their preferences at any time before the character assignment.

Recommended number of preferences:

  • 3 - 4 if the event has fewer than 30 characters
  • 5 - 6 if between 30 and 50 characters
  • 7 - 8 if more than 50 characters

If Show Statistics is checked, each unassigned character will display a graph showing how many participants have selected them as a preference.

Casting

When ready to assign characters, go to Event > Casting.

At the top of the page, you'll see a summary indicating if any participants have not submitted preferences or if any characters have received no preferences.

Note: The number of characters available for assignment is calculated as all characters minus those that received no preferences. If this number exceeds the number of participants who submitted preferences, the algorithm will fail.

You can select the list of ticket types, and the status of payment. If you have activated the Factions, you'll also find a selection on the characters to make available for assignment:

The list of participant preference is shown in the middle of the page:

The first column contains a selector to choose which participants to include in the assignment.
The second column shows the assignment priority based on the ticket selected by the participant.
The following columns display the list of each participant's character preferences.

By default, all preferences are active in the algorithm (YES). You can block a preference by clicking it, changing it to NO, which excludes it from consideration. Clicking again will reactivate it.

Clicking "Start Algorithm" runs a simulation of the assignment based on the current participant selections, preferences, and configuration data.

At then end of the page, you'll see the results of the simulation:

Review the simulation results carefully. When confirmed, click "Upload" to finalize and assign the characters.

If "Field for exclusions" is selected, an additional field will appear in the participant's preferences, allowing them to explicitly exclude certain themes.

This information will then be shown in the casting list, under the column "Avoid".

To make an informed decision on which character preferences to block for each participant, use the available data and distribution indicators.

For the algorithm to find a solution, preferences must be reasonably distributed among characters. If too many participants select the same few characters, the algorithm may fail.

In such cases, set a value for "Additional Preferences" in the configuration. This will assign each participant a random set of preferences from characters who received none, improving feasibility - but may result in some participants being assigned characters they did not choose.

Priority

You can assign a priority to each ticket type, giving participants with certain tickets a higher chance of receiving their preferred characters.

A new Casting priority field is now available in the ticket edit form.

If you can additionally tweak how the algorithm favours participants that:

  • Signed up earlier (Registration Priority option)
  • Paid in full earlier (Payment Priority option)

Both this options can be set: 0 (default disabled, not taken into consideration), 1 (normal priority), 10 (strong priority)

Mirror

If you want participants to select preferences while keeping characters secret, use the Mirror feature.

When this option is enabled, a new field, Mirror, appears on the character edit form, allowing you to define the mirrored version of the character that is shown to participants instead of the actual character.

Example: in your game, the baker is secretly the killer, but you want to hide this from participants. First create the public-facing character "The Baker", and then create another character "The Killer", and in its Mirror field, select "The Baker".

Participants who want to play the antagonist will submit preferences for "The Killer". If the casting algorithm assigns a participant to "The Killer", they will actually be assigned "The Baker".

Direct preferences for "The Baker" are ignored, preventing the character from being assigned to participants who did not explicitly choose to play the secret role.

Related tutorials: Matchmaker, Quests and Traits, Characters, Registration Ticket

name: Create Organization
descr:
This tutorial explains how to create your organization, the space where all your events live, and how to find your way around the management interface: the top bar, the sidebar and the help links.

To set up your organization, go to the Get started page and complete the creation form:

Organization settings

  • Name: The full name of your organization.
  • Logo: An optional image used as your organization's logo. You can upload any image format and size; it is scaled automatically.
  • Subdomain: The subdomain name for your organization. For example, if you choose "lp", all your pages are under https://lp.larpmanager.com. Use only letters and numbers - no spaces or symbols.
  • Payment currency: The currency used for all payments and pricing.

Click Submit to create your subdomain.

Upon submission, you are redirected to Organization > Dashboard. From this hub, you can create events, configure sessions, and access all organization-level tools.

Note: On first creation, the organization is in Lite Mode, where only basic functions are available. Complete the Activation Checklist to unlock Full Mode and access all features.

Note: the screenshots in these tutorials show an example organization, "Test Organization", with one event, "Test Event". In your pages you will see the names of your own organization and events.

At the top is the top bar, visible only to users with a management role in the organization or in one of its events. On the left, it shows the name of your organization and of the events you manage: click one to open its management pages.

On the right, the User / Admin switch moves between the management pages and the pages seen by participants:

On the left side of the page is the sidebar, with links to all the active functions of the organization or event you are managing:

On mobile, the left button opens the sidebar, and the right one the topbar:

If in the future you need to update the Organization, go to Organization > Organization.

Remember to access the LarpManager help pages if you need any help!

Organization features

LarpManager includes over 100 features, activated only when you need them. Some have an organization-wide scope, and apply to all pages and events of the organization; others have an event scope, and are active only for a specific event (see Manage Events).

To activate features for the whole organization, go to Organization > Features:

Click a feature's name to open a popup with its description. Select the features you want to activate and confirm.

Some features need further settings, in Organization > Configuration.

Related tutorials: Organization Roles, Organization Appearance, Manage Events, Personal Data

name: Personal Data
descr:
LarpManager can collect personal data from participants when they sign up for your events - such as address, date of birth, or fiscal code. This tutorial explains which fields are available, how to configure your organization's profile form, and what participants will see when filling it in.

Organization profile

When a user signs up for one of your events, LarpManager can collect and store specific personal data from them.

To choose which data to collect, go to Organization > Profile.

(Note that the first name and surname are stored by default.)

Here is a description of the available fields:

  • Portrait: A photo of the participant. Displayed in their public profile and in the game gallery.
  • Alias: By default, LarpManager displays a participant's first and last name in the event's public participant list. If a participant prefers not to show their real name, they can enter a nickname. (Their real name will still be visible to organizers and to other participants of the same event)
  • Pronouns: The participant's preferred pronouns, shown in their public profile.
  • Contact: A contact method for the participant (e.g., email, social media). Shown in the public profile.
  • Nationality, Phone Contact, Birth Date, Birth Place, Residence Address: Personal data not shown in the public profile.
  • First Aid: Indicates whether the participant is trained in first aid. Visible in the participant list for the game.
  • Document Type, Document Number, Date of issue, Date of expiration: The type, number and dates of an official identity document, based on the participant's country.
  • Diet: Dietary restrictions or needs. Visible only to selected organizers.
  • Safety: Information about physical or mental health. Visible only to selected organizers.
  • Legal Name: If the participant uses a name different from their legal name, the legal name can be entered here. It is used only for legal documents generated by LarpManager and is not visible to other participants.
  • Legal Gender: as it appears on official documents. It will only be used for internal bureaucratic purposes, and will NEVER be displayed to other participants.
  • Presentation: A short personal description, used in advanced features.

Note: If a participant previously provided this data when registering for an event from another organization using LarpManager, the data is pre-filled.

Sensitive data

You can review all participant data of each event in Event > Users.

Additionally, in Event > Registrations of each event, an eye icon appears next to each participant's name. Clicking the icon opens a popup displaying all available participant data (scrollable if the list is long).

Note: Sensitive data is visible only to users whose role includes the "Sensitive Data" permission.

Related tutorials: Users, Registrations, Membership

name: Organization Roles
descr:
Roles let you delegate platform management to other team members without giving them full access. Each role is a named set of permissions; users assigned to it can access only the areas you choose. This tutorial covers how to create roles and assign users to them.

Organization roles

To manage roles and grant permissions to other users, go to Organization > Roles.

An "Admin" role is automatically created and assigned to the user who created the organization. By default, this role has all permissions.

(Note: You can only add users to a role if they have granted permission to share their data with your organization. If the organization is newly created, the list is empty. You can invite them clicking on the invite icon.)

You can add users to an existing role by clicking the edit icon, or create a new role by clicking "New".

(Note: A user can be assigned to multiple roles. Their permissions are the combined total of all assigned roles)

Enter the role name in "Name", select the users to assign in "Members", and check the management pages they should have access to.

Note: Additional permissions will become available as you activate new features.

Inviting new users

To add someone who is not yet in the list, click the envelope icon on the role row and enter their email address. They receive an email with a link to accept the invitation; once they log in (or create an account) with that email address and agree to share their data with your organization, they are added to the role.

Pending invitations are shown under the role, until they are accepted.

Note: an invitation can be used only once, only by the email address it was sent to, and expires after some time.

Related tutorials: Event Roles, Create Organization, User Flags

name: Advanced features
descr:
Organization features

LarpManager includes over 100 advanced features covering all common aspects of LARP organization. Some features have an Organization-wide scope, and apply to all pages and events of the Organization. Others have an Event scope and are active only for a specific event.

In order to activate new features for the whole Organization, go to Organization > Features.

Click on a feature's name to open a popup with its description and a tutorial snippet.

Select the features you want to activate and confirm.

Some features may require additional configuration, available in Organization > Configuration.

Event features

In order to activate new features for a specific event, go to Event > Features.

The format of the page is the same as before. Some features may require additional configuration, available in Event > Configuration.

name: Event Roles
descr:
Event roles let you assign management permissions to collaborators for a specific event, without giving them access to the whole organization. This tutorial mirrors the organization roles system but scoped to a single event.

Event roles

To manage roles and grant permissions to other users on the event's functions, go to Event > Roles.

A role named "Organizer" is automatically created and assigned to the user who created the event. By default, this role has all permissions.

(Note: You can only add users to a role if they have granted permission to share their data with your organization. If the organization is newly created, the list is empty. You can invite them to the role by clicking the envelope icon)

You can add users to an existing role by clicking the edit icon, or create a new role by clicking "Add new".

(Note: A user can be assigned to multiple roles. Their permissions are the combined total of all assigned roles)

Enter the role name in "Name", select the users to assign in "Members", and check the management pages they should have access to.

Note: Additional permissions will become available as you activate new features.

Inviting new users

To add someone who is not yet in the list, click the envelope icon on the role row and enter their email address. They receive an email with a link to accept the invitation; once they log in (or create an account) with that email address and agree to share their data with your organization, they are added to the role.

Pending invitations are shown under the role, until they are accepted.

Note: an invitation can be used only once, only by the email address it was sent to, and expires after some time.

Related tutorials: Organization Roles, Manage Events

name: Event Appearance
descr:
Each event can have its own visual identity, independent of the organization-wide settings. This section lets you set a cover image, background, fonts, and colors specific to that event.

Event appearance

To customize the appearance of an event, go to Event > Appearance.

Input the following data:

  • Cover image: An image displayed on the Organization homepage as the event's cover.
  • Custom Title Font: A font file (TTF or OTF) used for all page titles.

If you select Halo (custom theme), additionally you can input:

  • Background Image: An image applied as a CSS background-cover on all event pages. Use an image with minimal detail and low color variation. Any size or format is accepted.
  • Text Color: The color used for all text. Ensure good contrast with the background image.
  • Background Color: The background color for text blocks. Ensure good contrast with both the text and background image.
  • Link Color: The color used for all hyperlinks.
  • Event CSS: Custom CSS code for the event. Contact support if you need the HTML structure for reference.

These customizations apply to all pages of the Event and override any Organization-level customizations.

Customize texts

You can also customize the texts that are used by LarpManager. To manage them, go to Event > Texts.

You can edit an existing one, or add a new one by clicking on "Add new".

Input the following data:

  • Text: The custom text content.
  • Type: The text type.
  • Language: The language in which the text is shown, based on the user's profile setting.
  • Default: Whether this version should be shown when no text exists for the user's selected language.

Only one version per language is allowed for each text type.

Only one version can be set as default for each text type.

Note: Additional text types will become available as you activate new features.

Customize navigation

You can customize the navigation buttons available to participants for the event by going to Event > Navigation.

You can edit an existing one, or add a new one clicking on "New".

Input the following data:

  • Name: the name that will appear on the navigation bar;
  • Tooltip: the text that will appear as the user hovers on the button;
  • Link: the link where the button will redirect the user once pressed;
  • Icon: the icon that is shown on the menu.

Here's an example:

Customize gallery

If the Characters feature is enabled, a "Gallery" tab becomes available in the event, showing all registered participants along with their associated characters. In Event > Configuration > Gallery, you can customize its visibility settings:

Related tutorials: Organization Appearance, Manage Events, Characters

name: Organization Appearance
descr:
This tutorial explains how to customize the visual identity of your organization's pages - background image, fonts, colors, and logo - so the platform matches your event brand. Changes apply across all pages of the organization.

Organization appearance

To customize the appearance of your organization, go to Organization > Appearance.

Input the following data:

  • Custom Title Font: A font file (TTF or OTF) used for all page titles.

If you select theme Halo (custom), you can additionally input:

  • Background Image: An image applied as a background on all pages using CSS background-cover. Use an image with minimal detail and low color variation. Any size or format is accepted.
  • Text Color: The color used for all text. Choose a color with good contrast against the background image.
  • Background Color: The background color for text blocks. Choose a color with good contrast against both the text and background image.
  • Link Color: The color used for all hyperlinks.
  • Association CSS: Custom CSS code. Contact support if you need the HTML structure to target.

Note: These settings apply to all pages under the Organization unless an Event has its own customized appearance.

Manage texts

You can also customize some of the texts that are used by LarpManager. To manage them, go to Organization > Texts.

You can edit an existing one, or add a new one by clicking on "New".

Input the following data:

  • Text: The custom text content.
  • Type: The type of text.
  • Language: The language for which this text is shown, based on the user's profile setting.
  • Default: Indicates whether this version should be shown if no text exists for the user's selected language.

Only one version per language is allowed for each text type.
Only one version can be set as default for each text type.

Calendar

In Organization > Configuration > Interface, you can control the advanced display options:

Checking those option, additional fields are added in the event creation form, and their value is shown in the calendar.

Carousel

Show your events in a scrolling gallery, like a streaming service. To use it, activate the Carousel feature.

Each event gets two new fields in Event > Event:

  • Carousel image: the image shown in the carousel.
  • Carousel description: a short text shown next to the image.

Legal notice

Add a legal notice page, linked from every page. To use it, activate the Legal Notice feature.

Then, in Organization > Texts, create a text of type "Legal notice" with its content. A "Legal Notice" link is added to the footer of every page.

Custom translations

Change how single words or sentences of the interface are written for your organization. To use it, activate the Translations feature.

Go to Organization > Translations and click "New":

  • Language: the language the translation applies to.
  • Original text: the English text as it appears in the interface.
  • Translated text: the text to show instead.
  • Context: optional, to tell apart the same text used with different meanings.
  • Active: uncheck to disable the translation without deleting it.

Related tutorials: Event Appearance, Create Organization, Mail Settings

name: Registrations
descr:
Event > Registrations is your central hub for tracking who has signed up for an event. From here you can review registration status, read registration question answers, manage payments, and handle cancellations.

Manage registrations

To view all participant registrations, head over to Event > Registrations.

If you have defined registration questions, a button for each will appear under "Registration Questions". Clicking on it will display the answer submitted by each signed-up participant.

By clicking on "Accounting", you can view a detailed breakdown of each registration's financial status, including amount owed, amount paid, total registration fee, portion from the ticket, and portion from selected options.

By clicking the edit icon, you can update the data for each registration. To add a new registration, click "New".

If the Characters feature is active (see the Characters tutorial), you can assign a character by entering its name in the Character field.

Cancellations

To cancel a registration from Event > Registrations, click the "Delete" icon. Participants will find the link to perform this action on their registration page.

You can manage the cancelled registrations in Event > Cancellations:

Additional tickets

To allow participants to register tickets in addition to theirs, activate the Additional tickets feature.

On the registration page, a new field, Additional, is added, where participants choose how many extra tickets to reserve.

The additional tickets reserved are counted upon the maximum allowed ones, and if the ticket has a price, they are added to the participant's registration fee.

Pre-registration

To allow participants to pre-register to events of their interest, activate the Pre-registration feature.

Then, for the events that you want to have the pre-registration active, go to Event > Event and you find a new value for the Registration Status:

Then in Event > Pre-Registrations you find the total list of pre-registrations, and the link to provide to participants to perform the pre-registration.

Secret registration link

If you wish to allow selected participants to sign up even when registrations are not publicly open, activate the Secret link feature.

In Event > Event, you find a new field, Secret registration code.

The field is pre-filled with a randomly generated code; if you wish you can insert another code (only english letters and digits allowed, no spaces or symbols).

Finally, copy the link to share with the participants from Event > Dashboard.

Related tutorials: Registration Ticket, Registration Form, Registration Accounting, Check-in

name: Manage Events
descr:
Events are the individual LARP sessions your organization runs. This tutorial explains how to create and configure them, setting dates, registration status, and appearance, as well as how to link events together into a campaign.

Create event

To create a new event, go to Organization > Events.

In this page, you can see all of your events. Click on "New event" to create a new one.

Event settings

Input the following values:

  • Name: The full name of the new Event.
  • URL Identifier: A simplified name used to build the URL of the event's pages. Use only letters and numbers; no spaces or symbols.
  • Description: A brief summary of the event (maximum 1000 characters).
  • Maximum participants: The maximum number of participants. Set to 0 for unlimited.
  • Template: Choose one of the basic event template, or leave empty for full configuration.
  • Start: the start date of the event;
  • End: the end date of the event (can be the same as start).
  • Status: the current status of the event. Can be Hidden (when a event is created but not announced), Visible (when a event is active), Cancelled (when a event has been announced but it is not active), and Concluded (when all the accounting has been completed). The event is not shown to the participants if the status is Hidden or Cancelled. The event is not shown in the organizer's quick bar, and it's accounting updated with the organization accounting, when the status is Cancelled or Concluded;
  • Registrations status: the registration status. Can be Closed (no new registrations are accepted), Open (new registrations are accepted, following the max participants limit), External (new registrations are handled through an external link, and a new field will appear to input this value - participants that are already enrolled, instead, will access their registration form), Open on date (registrations are accepted only from a given date and time forward), and Close on date (registrations are not accepted from a given date and time forward).

If you have activated the Characters feature, and the Field visibility configuration, in the form you can also control the visibility of specific writing elements to participants. These settings are session-specific, so you can choose to show these fields for one session and not for another.

If you select "Name", the list of writing elements is visible to participants; furthermore, for each field, you can select to display either to all participants (if the field is set as Public) or only to the participant assigned to that writing element (if the field is set as Private).

When you create a new event, your user is automatically assigned the Organizer role for that event.

You can also change the main event data directly from the event dashboard:

Participant pages

What participants see, and how they reach your events.

The home page of your organization, at https://<subdomain>.larpmanager.com/ (the subdomain chosen when creating the organization), lists the upcoming sessions, each with its name, dates and registration status:

A session is listed on the home page when:

  • its Status is Visible (a Hidden session is shown only to users already registered to it);
  • it is not Cancelled;
  • its end date has not passed yet.

To add a text at the top of the home page, create a text of type "Calendar" in Organization > Texts. To show more details on each card (location, website, authors, genre, tagline) or a link to past events, see the Organization Appearance tutorial.

Clicking on a session opens its event page, at https://<subdomain>.larpmanager.com/<URL identifier>/. It shows the registration status, the dates and the Description of the event:

Organizers can open it from Event > Dashboard, with the link icon next to the event name, or with the "User" switch in the top bar.

From the registration box of the event page, participants reach the registration page, where they choose a ticket and answer the registration questions:

Whether participants can sign up depends on the Registrations status of the session (see Event Settings above). To configure tickets and questions, see the Registration Ticket and Registration Form tutorials.

Note: to let selected people register to a session that is not yet public, share its secret link (see Secret registration link in the Registrations tutorial).

Event features

To activate features for a specific event, go to Event > Features:

The page works like the organization one (see Create Organization). Some features need further settings, in Event > Configuration.

Event sessions

An event can have multiple sessions (also called "runs" or "editions"), each with its own dates, registrations, and accounting, while sharing the main event configuration such as features, configurations, roles, tickets, forms, and other settings.

To create a new session of an existing event, go to Organization > Events and click on "New session".

Input the main Event, and the specific information of this new session.

Event template

To simplify event creation, define Event Templates. When creating a new event, you can select a template to automatically import its features, roles, and configuration.

First, activate the Template feature, then go to Organization > Template. Click on "New" to create a new one.

Select the Name of the template and the default features to activate for events created from it.

For each template, you can also set roles and configuration. Those settings are copied to all events created from it.

Those settings are copied to all events created from it.

Campaign

By default, characters belong to a single event, meaning each event has its own independent set. To share characters across multiple events, enable the Campaign feature. In Event > Event, there is a new field:

Here you can select a Campaign, i.e. a previous event that is used to link the new event. Events linked to the same Campaign will use the same character pool: any changes made to characters are reflected across all connected events. By designating one initial event and assigning it as the parent for subsequent events, you establish a Campaign structure with shared characters.

Note: If no other events exist, the Campaign field is not displayed.

Note: The events in the Campaign will also share features, and configurations. They will have different dates, locations, tickets, and options in the registration form.

Online events

For events held online, where participants do not need to be members to attend. Activate the LAOG feature on the event: the annual membership fee is not required, nor added to the registration fee, for that event.

Related tutorials: Event Roles, Event Appearance, Registrations, Registration Ticket

name: Registration Ticket
descr:
Tickets define the participation tiers available for an event: each with its own name, price, and maximum number of spots. This tutorial explains how to create tickets and control when and how participants can select them.

Manage tickets

To manage the event's registration tickets, go to Event > Tickets. Click on "New" to add a new ticket:

Input the following data:

  • Name: the name of the ticket;
  • Details: a short description of the ticket;
  • Price: the price of the ticket (shown in the currency defined in the Organization settings);
  • Total availability: the maximum number of registrations available with this ticket;
  • Visible: if the ticket is visible (and selectable) by the participants.

You can select different "tier" of tickets. To activate them, go to Event > Configuration > Tickets.

The ticket edit form has a new field, Tier:

Note: "Standard" is the default ticket tier for users / participants.

Note: The maximum number of available spots defined in the event does not include Staff tickets.

Here's an example of the selection for the participants:

Patron and reduced

With this feature, you can enable Reduced tickets, where availability is dynamically based on the number of Patron tickets previously selected by participants. First, activate the Patron and Reduced feature.

In Tier you find the two new types, Reduced and Patron.

In Event > Configuration > Patron / Reduced, you can configure the ratio between the two tickets:

At any moment, LarpManager calculates the total number of available Reduced tickets by multiplying the number of purchased Patron tickets by the defined ratio, dividing the result by 10, and rounding down.

Reserve

With this feature, you can enable "light" tickets, intended for a lighter experience, that works also as a "reserve" for the primary characters, if there is a dropout.

To use it, first activate the Reserve feature, then in Tier the new type Reserve is available.

Also in Event > Event you can set the total number of reserve spots in the Maximum reserves field.

When the number of registrations is below the Maximum participants, the Reserve ticket is not shown. Once the maximum is reached, all ticket types are disabled except for the Reserve tickets. When Reserve registrations also reach the defined Maximum reserves, registrations are closed.

Waiting list

With this feature you can have "waiting list" tickets. Once a regular ticket spot is available due to dropout, they can be upgraded. First, activate the Waiting list feature.

In Tier the new type Waiting is available.

Also in Event > Event you can set the total number of waiting list spots in the Maximum waiting list field.

When the number of registrations is below the Maximum participants, the Waiting ticket is not shown. Once the maximum is reached, all ticket types are disabled except for the Waiting tickets. When Waiting registrations also reach the Maximum Waiting List, registrations are closed.

Note: If both Reserve and Waiting tickets are activated, the order is as follows:

Up to the Maximum participants: all tickets are available, except Reserve and Waiting.
Between Participants and Reserve limits: only Reserve tickets are available.
Between Reserve and Waiting limits: only Waiting tickets are available.

Lottery

With this feature you can have a "lottery" system, where participants first sign up to participate in the lottery, and some of them are randomly selected to upgrade to a full ticket. To use it, activate the Lottery feature.

In Tier the new type Lottery is available.

In Event > Configuration > Lottery, you can configure the number of tickets to draw, and the regular ticket to upgrade to:

In Event > Lottery, you can perform the random selection. On first access, the extraction is executed and shown for confirmation. Upon confirmation, the selected tickets are upgraded.

New player tickets

A ticket reserved to people who have never attended an event of your organization, for example at a reduced price. To use it, activate the New player feature.

When creating a ticket, a new tier, New player, is available. The ticket is shown only to users without previous registrations to your events; registrations as waiting list, staff or NPC do not count.

Related tutorials: Registrations, Registration Accounting, Casting

name: Promotion
descr:
To promote your events, you can automatically export your event information to Larp aggregators:

  • LarpDatabase (ILDB): An international archive and search engine dedicated to Larp culture. The database contains organizations, events, authors, participants and many others to map and value the culture of LARP.
  • LarpRadar: An event discovery platform dedicated to LARPs, featuring an interactive map and a detailed calendar. It allows participants to discover events nearby, connect with other participants, and access community reviews.

Configuration

As a first step, enable the Promotion feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Promotion, configure the following values:

  • Publish staff: If checked, the list of staff members in each event role is shared as well;
  • Publish players: If checked, the list of participants with their character is shared as well (the nickname is used, if set, to protect folk's identities);
  • ILDB - API key: Insert the token generated on ILDB: go to "Change profile" / "Create API Token". Make sure to mark all permissions.
  • ILDB - Team ID: Insert the ID of your team / organization on ILDB. Can be found by looking at the url when accessing "Your organization", as the number after "https://www.larpdatabase.com/teams/".

Event data

In Event > Promotion, you can enter the information about your event to share:

When you press "Confirm", the data is automatically updated and shared.

ILDB

On LarpDatabase.com (ILDB), the event is created as draft. You can then review them and confirm their publication.

Related tutorials: Manage Events, Event Appearance

name: Registration Accounting
descr:
This tutorial covers the optional financial add-ons for the registration system: pay-what-you-want contributions, fixed installment plans, tokens, credits, and discount codes. Each is an independent feature you can activate selectively.

Pay what you want

To allow participant to add a free amount to their registration, activate the Pay what you want feature.

On the registration page, a new field, Pay what you want, is added, where participants can enter a free amount.

The indicated amount is added to the participant's registration fee.

If you wish, you can customize the name and description of the field in Event > Form.

Fixed instalments

With this feature, you can define multiple deadlines to split the payment of the registration fee into installments. First, activate the Fixed instalments feature.

Go to Event > Fixed instalments, and create a new payment deadline clicking on "New":

Define the following values:

  • Amount: The amount to be paid at this deadline. If set to 0 (typically for the final installment), LarpManager will request the remaining balance of the registration fee.
  • Days Deadline: Number of days from the moment of registration.
  • Date Deadline: A fixed calendar date for the deadline. (Only one between Days Deadline and Date Deadline is allowed and required)
  • Tickets: List of tickets the deadline applies to (Start typing in the input field to select).

Notes:

Defining both Days Deadline and Date Deadline is not allowed.

If no installments are defined for a ticket, the default payment deadline is 7 days from registration.

Dynamic rates

With this feature you can divide the payment of a registration fee in dynamic rates (or quotas). First, activate the Dynamic rates feature.

Go to Event > Dynamic rates, and create a new quota option clicking on "New":

Define the following values:

  • Quotas: The number of installments into which the payment is divided (e.g., 1 for full payment, 2 for two installments, 3 for three installments, etc.).
  • Days Available: The maximum number of days before the event when this option is available for new registrations. Set to 0 to make it always available.
  • Surcharge: An optional additional amount applied to this quota option.

For each quota option, the total registration fee is divided equally by the number of quotas. The first installment is due 7 days after registration. Remaining installments are scheduled by dividing the time between registration and event start by the number of quotas.

Participants will select their preferred quota option at registration, from those available at that time.

Example: define 3 payment options; quotas 2 and 3 have day limits (to prevent multi-tranche payments for last-minute registrations), and quota 3 includes a surcharge to account for increased accounting workload.

Assuming a total registration fee of 100 and a registration 60 days before the event:

  • 1 quota: 100 due 7 days after registration
  • 2 quotas: 50 due 7 days after registration, 50 due 30 days after registration
  • 3 quotas: 33 due 7 days after registration, 33 due 20 days, 34 due 40 days after registration

Note: The quota options are applied to to all registrations and tickets.

If you wish, you can customize the name and description of the field in Event > Form.

Registration surcharges

With this feature, a surcharge is automatically added to a registration if it is created after a defined deadline. First, activate the Surcharge feature.

Go to Event > Surcharges, and create a new surcharge option clicking on "New":

Indicate the Amount of the surcharge, and the deadline Date. The surcharge is added to all registrations created after the deadline.

Discount

With this feature you can provide discount codes to the participants. First, activate the Discount feature.

Go to Event > Discounts, and create a new discount clicking on "New":

Define the following values:

  • Name: Internal name of the discount.
  • Sessions: Sessions where the discount is active.
  • Value: Amount deducted from the total registration fee.
  • Max redeem: Maximum number of times this discount can be used.
  • Code: Discount code participants must enter (customizable).
  • Type: Type of discount - Standard or Play Again (usable only if the participant has already participated in another session of the same event).
  • Visible: Whether the discount is visible and usable by participants.
  • Only reg: If enabled, the discount can be used only during registration creation, not on later updates.

A field will appear in the registration form where participants can enter a discount code, which will then be reserved for 15 minutes.

Gift

With this feature, participants can reserve registrations, complete payment, and later assign them as gifts to other participants. First, activate the Gift feature.

A new checkbox, Giftable, is added to both tickets and registration questions.

Only Tickets and Questions marked as giftable will appear as options in the gift registration form.

Participants will now find a new page, "Gift", in the event menu.

By clicking "Add new", participants can create new registrations. These count toward ticket and option limits, allowing them to be booked. In Event > Registrations, they are marked with the gift icon.

When a gift registration is paid, a special link is generated. Another participant can access the link to claim the registration, provided they do not already have a registration for that session. Once claimed, the registration is no longer marked as "gift".

Bring a friend

Reward participants who bring new people to your events. To use it, activate the Bring a friend feature.

In Event > Configuration > Bring a friend, set the two discounts:

  • Referrer Reward Discount: discount given to the participant whose code was used.
  • Referred Friend Discount: discount given to the new participant who registers with the code.

After registering, each participant receives by email a personal code to share. A friend enters it in the Code 'Bring a friend' field of the registration form, and both get their discount.

Related tutorials: Payments, Accounting, Registration Ticket

name: Payments
descr:
The Payments feature enables online payment collection directly through the platform. When active, registrations with a non-zero fee start in a provisional state and are confirmed only after the first payment. This tutorial covers gateway configuration, payment status management, and refunds.

Payments

To receive payments from your participants, activate the Payments feature.

Note: When this feature is active, and the participant has a non-zero registration fee, the registration is not immediately confirmed; it is instead provisional, and is confirmed only upon the first payment.

You now need to configure the payment settings. LarpManager supports multiple payment gateways, each requiring its own specific configuration.

You will now find a new page, Organization > Methods:

Select the gateway you wish to activate. For each activated gateway, new fields will appear to input the required data specific to that gateway. Each gateway has its own set of fields, explained in its section.

For Fee, enter the percentage of the amount that is going to be witheld by the gateway. Enter the value as a number without the percentage symbol: for example, for a 1.5% fee, input: 1.5.

After registration, participants are automatically redirected to a page where they can select a payment method. Both the participant's and the event's accounting are updated automatically.

Note: Wire payment requires participants to upload a proof of payment, which must then be manually approved by the event staff from the pending payments list at the top of Event > Payments.

It will then be possible to review all received payments either in Organization > Payments, or in Event > Payments.

Additional configuration

As an additional configuration, in Organization > Configuration > Payments you find:

  • Charge transaction fees to participant: If checked, the fees witheld by the payment gateway are added to the user. If the fee is 3%, and the total registration fee is 150€, the user is asked to pay 154.64€ (as that is the amount that minus 3% gives 150€).
  • Disable amount change: By default, participants can edit the payment amount (e.g., split €100 into two €50 payments). Enabling this option disables that flexibility.
  • Unique Code: A unique code is added automatically to each registration's payment description. For example, "Registration fee of Elena Ricci for Test Event" becomes "Registration fee of Elena Ricci for Test Event - hR04SlbZOPXFzFx". This code helps with automatic payment validation by uniquely identifying the registration.
  • Require receipt for manual payments: If selected, when confirming the payment done with a wire payment, the user is also asked to upload a payment receipt.

And also, for each event, in Event > Configuration > Payments you find:

  • Payment reminder: If fixed or dynamic rates are selected, LarpManager will treat all payments with a deadline earlier than the specified value as urgent and notify the user accordingly.
  • Payment reference: By default, the payment justification is formatted like "Registration fee of Elena Ricci for Test Event". You can customize this by entering a template string; for example, inputting "Thanks {player_name} for your help!" will result in "Thanks Elena Ricci for your help!".
  • Disable provisional registrations: By default, registrations are marked as "provisional" unless a payment is performed. If this option is enabled, no registration are marked provisional, and are immediately confirmed.

Related tutorials: Registration Accounting, Accounting, Membership

name: Registration Form
descr:
Registration questions let you collect custom information from participants at registration time: multiple and single choice answers, long and shor text, and more. This tutorial shows how to create, configure, and order them.

Manage questions

To manage the event's registration questions, go to Event > Form.

Those are questions that the participants can answer during registration.

You can edit the existing questions, or you can add a new one by clicking on "New".

Input the following data:

  • Type: can be Single choice, Multiple choice, Single-line text, Multi-line text, Advanced text editor (rendered as a WYSIWYG editor), Likert scale;
  • Name: the label that is shown for the question;
  • Description: the text that is shown as help text under the question;
