  • Status: can be Optional (active but not required), Mandatory (active and required), Disabled (shown but not editable), Hidden (not shown).
  • Maximum length: the maximum length of the text, or the maximum amount of choices.

Here's an example of a Single-line text:

Here's an example of a Multi-line text:

Here's an example for Advanced Text Editor (click on "Show" to show it):

And here's an example of the Likert scale:

Manage options

Fo Single choice and Multiple choice you also need to define the options. You find the list of the options, and the link to add a new one, directly when editing the question:

Input the following data:

  • Name: the text that is shown for this option;
  • Description: an optional description (shown in the help text of the question);
  • Price: the price that this option will add to the registration fee (if 0, it is not shown);
  • Maximum: the maximum number of registrations with this option (if 0, there is no limit).

Here's an example of Single choice and Multiple choice question:

If you want to reorder either questions or options, hold on the 6-points icon on the left.

Sections

To organize the questions in the registration form in sections, first activate the Sections feature.

In Event > Sections, you can create the sections:

Then, in the edit form of each question, choose its section in the Section field.

In the participant's registration form, the sections are shown as collapsible parts (by clicking on the header, the section questions are shown or hidden).

Additional configurations

In Event > Configuration > Registrations, you can find the following configurations:

Here's an explanation:

  • Disable grouping: By default, registrations are displayed in different tables given their status; when this configuration is enabled, they are instead shown in a single table;
  • Allowed: When enabled, each registration question gets a field where you choose which staff members can see the participants' answers to it.
  • Hide Not Available: By default, options that have reached their selection limit appear disabled. If this option is enabled, they are hidden entirely.
  • Faction Selection: Adds a "Factions" field to each registration question. If filled, the question is shown only to participants assigned a character from one of the selected factions.
  • Ticket Selection: Adds a "Tickets" field to each registration question. If filled, the question is shown only to participants who selected one of the specified ticket types.
  • Age Selection: Adds a "Minimum Age" field to each registration question. If set, the question is shown only to participants who meet or exceed the specified age.
  • Disable cancellation: If enabled, participants cannot directly cancel their own registration; if they press than button, a request will instead be sent to the organizers, that can manually cancel it.
  • Approval process: see next paragraph.

Approval process

If the configuration is enabled in Event > Configuration > Registrations, then participants cannot directly sign up to the event.

On registration page, a new participant will find this instead:

A new page is available, Event > Requests. Here organizers can review the requests; if one is approved, then that participant is allowed to proceed with the normal registration form.

Related tutorials: Registrations, Registration Ticket, Matchmaker, Debrief

name: Characters
descr:
Characters are the in-game personas that participants embody at your event. This tutorial covers how staff creates and manages them, how the character numbering and cross-reference system works, and how to control what participants can see.

Manage characters

To manage the event's characters, first activate the Characters feature, then go to Event > Characters.

You can edit the existing characters, or you can add a new one by clicking on "Add new".

Input the following data:

  • Name: the name of the character;
  • Presentation: a short description of the character, visible to all participants;
  • Text: a long description of the character, visible only to the participant to which the character is assigned.

(For Presentation and Text click on "Show" to display the input field).

To define additional fields see the Character Sheet tutorial.

Gallery and search

Participants browse the event's characters from two pages, linked in the event navigation bar: Gallery and Search.

  • Gallery shows the character portraits, each linking to the character's page. Characters are grouped under their primary faction (see the Factions tutorial). At the bottom, under Registrants, it lists the participants that do not have a character yet (staff, NPC, collaborator, seller and waiting list tickets are excluded, as are provisional registrations).
  • Search lets participants filter the characters and read their public information in one page. The buttons at the top open the filters:
  • Instructions: how the filters work;
  • Search: free text, matched on the character's number, name, presentation, participant and groups;
  • Status: show only characters already assigned to a participant;
  • Factions: filter by faction (shown when the event has more than one faction);
  • one button for each character field with visibility Searchable, to filter by its options;
  • Characters link: the list of all character names, each linking to its page.

Click a filter value once to include it (characters in at least one included value are shown), and a second time to exclude it (characters in any excluded value are hidden).

To make a character field available as a Search filter, set its Visibility to "Searchable" in Event > Sheet (see the Character Sheet tutorial).

To add an introduction at the top of the Search page, go to Event > Texts, click "New" and select the type "Search".

In Event > Configuration > Gallery you can limit who sees the characters:

  • Require login: characters are hidden from visitors that are not logged in.
  • Require registration: characters are hidden from users not registered to the event.
  • Hide unassigned characters: characters without a participant are not shown in the gallery.
  • Hide participants without a character: the Registrants list is not shown.

Note: which character fields are shown in both pages depends on the visibility set in Event > Event, see Characters configuration below.

Characters configuration

In Event > Configuration > Characters you find those options:

  • Field visibility: If you want more fine-grained control over which fields are visible to the participant at each moment, click this option and then see the next section.
  • Played characters: You can select the number of character the participants will play in the game (default 1).
  • Disable Character Finder: If you don't want the character finder, you can disable it here.
  • Replacing Names: In the character fields, existing character names are automatically replaced by references like #<number>.
  • Paste as Text: In the WYSIWYG editor, pasted content is stripped of formatting.
  • Disable Auto Save: By default, writing elements are saved automatically while you edit them, so no work is lost, and you are warned if two users edit the same element at the same time. Enable this option to turn both off.
  • External Access: If you want to allow any user to access the complete sheet of a character, enable this option. In the characters' page, a key icon will appear next to the character's name, with the link to share to allow to do so.
  • Unimportant: Activates a special tracking of plots or relationships that are less important to the character.
  • Check: If enabled, a new page is available in the event dashboard, allowing to check consistency of references between characters (see Checking references in the Character References tutorial below).
  • Reading: If enabled, a new special page is available in the Event's management, allowing staff to access characters with read-only access.

Field visibility

If in your event the character's sheet are written by the staff, with this configuration you can control exactly what participants are able to see at any moment.

You can do it in Event > Event:

The selected elements are shown to participants only if checked.

(Characters are visible only if Name is selected)

References and PDF

To mention other characters by their number in any text, and check that these references are consistent, see the Character References tutorial.

To print character sheets and the character gallery as PDF, with your own layout, see the PDF Generation tutorial.

Single field edit

You can edit a character's field directly by double-clicking on it. This opens a popup allowing you to edit the field without opening the full character editor.

Relationships

Allows staff to define inter-character relationships. To use it, activate the Relationships feature.

At the end of the character edit form, you can now define relationships. At the end of the character edit form, you can select another character to add one:

The field labeled "Direct" is used to write the character's relationship toward another. If the other character has a relationship defined toward this one, it will appear under "Inverse".

The list of relationships is shown to the participant at the end of the character's page.

Character customization

With this feature, participants can customize some elements for the specific session they've signed up for. To use it, activate the Character customization feature.

Note: Customization applies only to the session where the participant is signed up. In events with multiple sessions, participants can customize their character independently for each session.

In Event > Configuration > Character customisation, you can select which fields are allowed for customization. Only the chosen fields are available for participants to edit during their character customization process.

On their assigned character, participants will find this button:

Clicking it opens the form where the selected customizable fields can be filled in by the participant.

Related tutorials: Character Sheet, Character Creation, Factions, Plots

name: Character Sheet
descr:
Character fields let you add custom attributes to characters beyond the defaults: group affiliation, status, mana, or any other value you need to track. This tutorial shows how to create, order, and configure them.

Manage fields

You can add any number of character fields, to track characteristics of them, such belonging to a group, special status or the amount of their mana. To manage the character fields, go to Event > Sheet.

You can edit existing fields or add a new one by clicking "New".

Input the following data:

  • Type: can be Single choice, Multiple choice, Single-line text, Multi-line text, Advanced Text Editor (rendered as a WYSIWYG editor)
  • Name: the label that is shown for the question;
  • Description: the text that is shown as help text under the question;
  • Visibility: can be Searcheable (shown as filter in gallery and search tabs), Public (visible by all participants), Private (visibile only by the assigned participant), Hidden (visible only to the staff).
  • Printable: whether the field should be included in the PDF output.

If the Character creation feature is active (see the Character Creation tutorial), an additional field will appear, specifying how the field should be handled when the participant edits or creates their character:

  • Status: can be Optional (active but not required), Mandatory (active and required), Disabled (shown but not editable), Hidden (not shown in the form).
  • Name: Text shown for this option.
  • Description: Optional help text displayed under the question.

If you want to reorder either questions or options, click and drag on the leftmost icon.

Configurations

In Event > Configuration > Character Sheet, you find four options:

  • Hide Not Available: When enabled, character options that are not available due to restrictions are hidden entirely instead of shown as disabled. If disabled, unavailable options are visible but not selectable.
  • Maximum Available: Adds a field to set the maximum number of times an option can be selected across all characters (applies to both Single and Multiple choice fields).
  • Ticket Selection: Adds a field to restricts an option's availability to characters assigned to participants who selected specific tickets. If no tickets are set, the option is available for all.
  • Requirements: Adds a field to restricts option availability based on other selected options. Requires all fields listed (AND) and at least one of the specified options within each field (OR). Applies to both Single and Multiple choice fields.
  • Title: If enabled, a special field "title" is available (see Title below), and it's content is shown together with the character's name in the gallery.
  • Number: If enabled, each character is assigned an unique numerical ID; see the Character References tutorial.
  • Cover image: If enabled, a cover image can be uploaded for each character (see Cover below), shown in the gallery until the character is assigned to a participant.
  • File: If enabled, in the character sheet there is available a special "file" field, useful for uploading PDFs, images or other files.
  • Hide: If enabled, each character will have an "Hide" field, with which it can be hidden from participants.
  • Locked: If enabled, each character gets a Locked checkbox; when it is checked, the private fields of that character are not shown to the assigned participant.
  • Assignment: If enabled, each will have an "Assigned" field (see Assigned below), where a staff member can be selected as the assigned author for that character.

Title

Used to add a short 2-3 word title to characters. A new field, Title, is added to the character form.

The title will appear in the gallery next to the character's name.

Cover

Allows customization of the character's cover image (before assignment to a participant). A new field, Cover, is added to the character form.

The cover image is displayed in the gallery.

Assigned

Tracks which staff member is responsible for a writing element (character, faction, etc). A new field, Assigned, is added to the character form.

The member list is drawn from users with a staff role in the event.

Progress

This field is used to track the writing progress of a writing element (example: draft, review, approved, etc). To use it, activate the Progress feature.

Go to Event > Progress, and add new progress steps clicking on "Add".

A new field, Progress, is added to the character form.

If both Progress and Assigned are active, a summary appears mapping assigned characters to progress.

Related tutorials: Characters, Character Creation, Experience Points

name: Character Creation
descr:
With the character creation feature, participants can create and edit their own characters directly on the platform. This tutorial explains how to configure the maximum character limit, the approval workflow, and what the creation flow looks like from the participant's perspective.

Character creation

With this feature, characters can be created and edited by the participants. To use it, activate the Character creation feature.

In Event > Configuration > Character creation, these options are available:

Maximum Number

The Maximum Number option sets the limit of characters a participant can create:

If set to 0, the participant cannot create characters but can edit characters created by staff and assigned to them.

If set to a value greater than 0, and the participant is signed up and currently has fewer characters than the limit, they are prompted to create a new character.

After a character is created, new links are added to the sidebar to open the character page or edit it:

Note: When a character is created by the participant, it is automatically assigned to them for that event.

Note: If the Campaign feature is active, and the participant created a character in the parent event, signing up to a new event will automatically assign that character to them in the new event as well.

Approval

You can setup a character approval process, requiring each character to be submitted by the participant and approved by staff before joining.

Check the Approval option; a Status field is added when editing characters in Event > Characters.

The possible values are:

  • Creation: Character has been created.
  • Proposed: Participant has submitted the character for staff approval.
  • Review: Staff has requested changes.
  • Approved: Character has been approved.

On the participant's character form, only if the character is in status Creation, there is this link available:

If confirmed, the character moves to Proposed.

Characters appear in the gallery only when Approved.

Custom texts for each status change can be defined in Event > Texts, by selecting the appropriate type.

Additionally, each character field in Event > Sheet can be configured to be editable only in selected stages:

Important: This feature is designed for single-session events. For multi-session events (where a character is played by different participants in different sessions), use Character Customization instead.

Active / inactive characters

This feature is only available when the Campaign feature is active.

In a campaign, a character may become permanently retired, killed, or otherwise unable to continue. You can reflect this by marking them as Inactive.

To do so, open the character's edit form from Event > Characters. When Campaign is active, an Active checkbox will appear.

By default, all characters are Active. Uncheck the box to mark the character as Inactive:

  • The character can no longer be manually or automatically assigned to a participant (assignments for events that have not yet started are automatically deleted)
  • Inactive characters are not counted toward the participant's maximum character limit. This allows the participant to create or receive a new character without hitting the cap.

In Event > Characters, an Active column is shown (toggle it from the column selector). A checkmark indicates the character is active; no checkmark means inactive.

Similarly, from the participant's side, the Characters page groups campaign characters by campaign and shows an Active column. A checkmark means the character is still in play; no checkmark means the character is retired.

Note: Inactive characters remain visible, so their character sheet and game history is maintained.

Player relationships

This feature allows participants to write relationships between their character and others. To use it, activate the Player relationships feature.

A "Relationship" button is added on the user's side:

Clicking "New" opens the relationship form.

Relationships are listed at the end of the character's page.

Related tutorials: Characters, Character Sheet, Casting

name: Character Inventory
descr:
The Character inventory feature lets you assign and track resources, such as currencies, materials, or consumables, to characters. Staff can define resource types, create inventories, add resources from the NPC bank, and track every transfer. Participants can view their inventory on their character sheet and transfer resources to other characters at any moment.

Setup: pool types

Before creating inventories, define the types of resources characters can hold. To do this, go to Event > Pool Types and click "Add" to create a new resource type.

Set as Name the name of the resource (e.g. "Money", "Weapons", "Reagents").

Note: all pool types you define here will appear as separate balance rows in every inventory.

Inventories

Go to Event > Character Inventory to see all inventories for the event. A character can own multiple inventories, and an inventory can be shared by multiple characters.

Note that a personal inventory for each character is created automatically for each character. It is named <Character Name>'s Personal Storage and is assigned to that character as its sole owner. This means you do not need to create individual inventories manually for every character, as they are provisioned automatically.

To create a new Inventory (for example for a bank or a guild), click "New". Define the following values:

  • Name: a label for the inventory.
  • Owners: one or more characters that have access to this inventory.

Viewing and managing an inventory

From Event > Character Inventory, click the view icon next to an inventory to open its detail page.

The first section is Currencies & Materials, with a row for each pool type with the current balance. Staff can add resources directly from the NPC bank by entering an amount and clicking "Add from NPC". A Reason field is available to record why the resources were added. The source inventory must have enough resources (transfers that exceed the available balance are rejected).

Note: Staff can transfer from any inventory to any other inventory, or from/to the NPC bank. Participants can transfer only from inventories they own, and cannot transfer to or from the NPC bank.

Note: "NPC" in the transfer log means the event's resource bank; it represents resources entering or leaving the game economy.

The second section is Transfer Log: a full history of every transfer involving this inventory, showing the time, the staff member or participant who performed the transfer, the source and target inventories, the resource type, the amount, and the reason.

Participant view

On the participant's character sheet, an Inventories section appears listing all inventories owned by that character. Each inventory card shows the name and the current balance of every resource type, with a link to the inventory detail page.

Participants can open the detail page to view their transfer history and send resources to other characters' inventories.

Related tutorials: Characters, Experience Points

name: Experience Points
descr:
The Experience points feature lets you assign XP to characters and allow participants to spend it on abilities and skills. This tutorial explains how to configure the XP system, manage ability trees, and handle participant-driven selection.

Abilities

With the feature active, first define the type of abilities in Event > Ability type, and click on "Add" to input a new type of ability.

Go to Event > Abilities, and click on "Add" to input a new ability:

  • Name: Name of the ability;
  • Type: The associated ability type;
  • Cost: XP cost to acquire the ability (If the cost is 0, the ability is automatically given to the characters).
  • Description: Explanation of what the ability does;
  • Pre-requisites: List of other abilities that a character is required to have for this ability to be available;
  • Requirements: List of character options (see the Character Sheet tutorial) that a character is required to have for this ability to be available;
  • Characters: List of characters to assign this ability to.

Awards

To give experience points to characters, go to Event > Awards, and click on "Add":

Input the name for the award, the amount of experience points to give, and the list of characters to select.

You can also directly load characters from all participants that participated in the event:

(Abilities and awards for each character can be selected also in the characters's edit form)

Configurations

In Event > Configuration > Experience points, these options are available:

  • Player selection: allows participants to add abilities themselves to their characters, see Player Selection below.
  • Undo period: Grace period to allow participants to change their idea on chosen ability, removing them and getting back its XP cost. (default is 0).
  • Initial experience points: Value of experience points added by default to all characters.
  • Ability templates: see Templates below.
  • Rules: see Rules below.
  • Modifiers: see Modifiers below.
  • Criteria: see Criterions below.
  • Auto buy: enforce automatic buy of all abilities available if there are available XP on a character.
  • Disable free abilities: by default, character automatically acquire abilities with 0 cost. With this configuration, this is disabled.
  • Multiple systems: see System below.

Player selection

If Player Selection is checked, participants will see a new page on their character page:

Where they can obtain new abilities, provided they have sufficient XP and meet all prerequisites:

If you have set a value of Undo Period, participants can cancel a newly acquired ability for that number of hours:

When defining new abilities, you find a new checkbox, Visible.

Participants can obtain only abilities that are: 1) visible, 2) for which they have all the required pre-requisites (AND between pre-requisite abilities), 3) for which they have chosen the indicated character options (as defined here - AND between character fields, OR within each character field)

Rules

You can also configure custom character fields whose value is auto-computed based on the character's abilities; for example, hit points. To configure them, first enable Rules in Event > Configuration > Experience points, then go to Event > Sheet and create a new character field with type "Computed" (this field is not editable by staff or the participant, as it's value is automatically computed):

Go to Event > Rules to define how this new field should be computed:

Set as values:

  • Abilities: The rule is applied for all characters with at least one of the abilities. If no abilities are selected, the rule is applied to all character. (Please note that the rule is applied only one time; if you want separate effects for different abilities, add new rules for them).
  • Field: The character field whose value is updated.
  • Operation: Either addition, subtraction, multiplication, division.
  • Amount: The value of the operation.

Modifiers

You can define alternative costs for abilities, based on whether the character has already learned certain abilities or meets specific character conditions, for example:

  • Assign default skills for a class by setting their cost to 0, so all characters of that class automatically gain them.
  • Reduce the cost of a skill for a class, meaning it's easier for them to obtain;
  • Block certain skills by assigning a prohibitive cost (e.g., 999) if the character has already learned conflicting abilities or belongs to a restricted class.

Note: If multiple modifiers apply to the same ability, only the first one in the defined order takes effect.

To manage them, first enable them in Event > Configuration > Experience points, then go to Event > Modifiers to define how this new rule should be applied:

Set as values:

  • Abilities: The modifier is applied to all the selected abilities.
  • Cost: The new cost to apply.
  • Pre-requisites: The modifier is applied if the character has learnt all of the selected pre-requisite abilities.
  • Requirements: The modifier is applied if the character has all the selected options (see Manage fields in the Character Sheet tutorial).

Criterions

You can define conditions that alters the amount of experience points for a character, given any combination of character options, or even pre-requisite abilities. For example, a specific race that starts with less experience points, or a specific combination of abilities that conveys an experience bonus.

To configure them, enable them in Event > Configuration > Experience points, then go to Event > Criteria.

System

LarpManager automatically creates one system for experience points (with name "XP"). You can manage multiple systems, each one with their dedicated abilities and deliveries.

To configure them, enable them in Event > Configuration > Experience points, then go to Event > Systems.

Templates

If you have a lot of similar abilities, you can set up the Template. If in a ability you set a template, will use its description; so if you set up many abilities with the same template, they will all share the same description, while having different costs and requirements.

To configure them, enable them in Event > Configuration > Experience points, then go to Event > Ability Templates.

Related tutorials: Characters, Character Sheet, Check-in, Debrief

name: Debrief
descr:
This tutorial explains how to collect feedback from participants after the event with a debrief form, and how to review their answers. Use it to learn what worked, what to improve, and whether participants want to come back.

Activating debrief

To use it, activate the Debrief feature.

A new page, Event > Debrief answers, becomes available in the event dashboard, and a new form type, Debrief, is added to Event > Form.

Debrief questions

Go to Event > Form and select Debrief next to "Configure form". Click "New" to add a question.

Debrief questions work like the questions of the registration form: you can use single-line and multi-line text, single and multiple choice, and Likert scale questions, each with a name, a description and a status (see the Registration Form tutorial).

Tip: a Likert scale question (for example an overall rating from 1 to 5) gives you a chart of the answers; a multi-line question collects free comments.

Participant view

Every participant with a confirmed registration finds a new entry, Debrief, in the event menu:

The page shows the debrief questions. Answers are kept as a draft while the participant types, and are submitted by clicking "Save". Participants can come back later to change their answers.

Note: participants without a registration, or with a registration request still pending, are asked to register first.

Reviewing the answers

Go to Event > Debrief answers. The table lists every participant who answered at least one question, with a column for each question; use the search and the column filters to find specific answers.

Below the table, each Likert scale question has a chart with the number of participants for each value:

Reminding participants

This requires the Deadlines feature to also be active (see the Deadlines tutorial).

Once the session is over, Event > Deadlines lists the participants who have not filled the debrief yet, with their emails and a link to the debrief page to send them:

Experience points for feedback

This requires the Experience points feature to also be active (see the Experience Points tutorial).

To reward the participants who filled the debrief, go to Event > Awards, open the Load characters menu and select From participants who filled the debrief.

The new award form is pre-filled with the characters of those participants; set the amount of points and save.

Related tutorials: Registration Form, Experience Points, Deadlines

name: Guilds
descr:
Guilds are groups of characters created and managed by the participants themselves: a thieves' guild, a band of mercenaries, a secret circle. This tutorial explains how participants create guilds and invite other characters, and what organizers can see and configure.

Activating guilds

To use it, activate the Guilds feature. It requires the Characters feature (see the Characters tutorial).

In Event > Configuration > Guilds you can set two limits:

  • Maximum number: how many guilds participants can create in the event (0 = no limit).
  • Maximum members: how many accepted members each guild can have (0 = no limit).

Creating a guild

Participants find a new entry, Guilds, in the event menu:

The page lists the guilds of the event with their members, and has the links to create a new guild and to see pending invites:

Any participant with a character can create a guild, until the maximum number is reached. In the creation form they choose which of their characters founds the guild (and becomes its first admin), then set:

  • Name, Presentation (visible to everyone) and Text (visible to members only).
  • Guild cover: the guild logo.
  • Secret: if checked, the guild is not shown in the guild list or in the gallery; only its members see it.

Members and roles

The guild page shows its presentation and members. Admins are marked with a star.

Guild admins can:

  • Invite a character playing in the event, from the invite box at the bottom of the page;
  • Promote to admin a member, or Remove admin from an admin;
  • Remove from guild a member;
  • Edit the guild details.

Invited participants find the invite in My pending invites, where they can accept or decline it:

The guild admins are notified by email when an invite is accepted or declined. A member can leave the guild at any time; the last admin must promote another member before leaving.

Note: invites can only be accepted while the guild is below its maximum number of members.

Guilds in the gallery

Non-secret guilds are shown in the character gallery, each with its members:

Managing guilds

Organizers can see and edit every guild, including the secret ones, in Event > Guilds:

To add custom fields to guilds, go to Event > Sheet (see the Character Sheet tutorial).

Related tutorials: Factions, Characters

name: Matchmaker
descr:
The matchmaker collects what each participant would like to play, before characters are assigned: the kind of role, the factions they prefer, how much intrigue or combat they want. This tutorial explains how to set up the matchmaker questions and review the answers.

Activating matchmaker

To use it, activate the Matchmaker feature.

A new page, Event > Matchmaker answers, becomes available in the event dashboard, and a new form type, Matchmaker, is added to Event > Form.

Matchmaker questions

Go to Event > Form and select Matchmaker next to "Configure form". Click "New" to add a question.

Matchmaker questions work like the questions of the registration form: single-line and multi-line text, single and multiple choice, and Likert scale (see the Registration Form tutorial).

A question of type Faction preference is created automatically: participants drag the factions of the event into their order of preference. This type is available only in the matchmaker form, once.

Participant view

Every participant with a confirmed registration finds a new entry, Matchmaker, in the event menu:

The page shows the matchmaker questions. Answers are kept as a draft while the participant types, and are submitted by clicking "Save". Participants can come back later to change their answers.

Reviewing the answers

Go to Event > Matchmaker answers. The table lists every participant who answered, with a column for each question; faction preferences are shown as a ranked list.

Below the table, each Likert scale question has a chart with the number of participants for each value:

Use these answers to write or assign the characters; for an assignment based on character preferences, see the Casting tutorial.

Related tutorials: Casting, Registration Form, Factions

name: User Flags
descr:
User flags are custom yes/no markers that organizers set on users: signed the code of conduct, qualified first aider, volunteer this year. This tutorial explains how to define the flags, set them for each user, and where they are shown.

Activating user flags

In Organization > Configuration > Users, enable User flags:

Two new pages become available in the organization dashboard: Organization > Flags types and Organization > User flags.

Flag types

Go to Organization > Flags types and click "New" to define a flag:

  • Name: short name, shown as column header.
  • Description: shown as a tooltip on the column header.
  • Annual: if enabled, the flag resets every calendar year instead of staying permanent (useful for yearly checks, like a volunteer shift). It cannot be changed after the flag is created.

Setting the flags

Go to Organization > User flags. The table shows every user of the organization, with a column for each flag; use the column filters to find, for example, the users missing a flag.

Click the edit icon on a row to change the flags of that user, then click "Save":

Where flags are shown

The flags of a user are shown to organizers when they open the participant details from the eye icon in Event > Registrations, and in the pending payments to approve:

Note: flags are visible only to organizers; users never see them.

Related tutorials: Users, Membership

name: Writing Extras
descr:
Besides characters, plots and factions, LarpManager can manage other writing elements for your event: prologues, handouts, speed larp scenes and workshops. This tutorial covers each of them.

Prologues

Short introductory texts, one for each act or moment of the event, given to the characters involved. To use it, activate the Prologues feature.

First create at least one prologue type (for example "Act I") in Event > Prologue types:

Then create the prologues in Event > Prologues:

  • Typ: the prologue type.
  • Name: name of the prologue.
  • Text: the prologue itself.
  • Characters: the characters who receive it.

Participants read their prologues in their character page.

Handouts

Documents about a plot or the lore, printed as PDF with your own layout. To use it, activate the Handout feature.

First create a handout model in Event > Handout Models: its CSS defines the page layout (size, margins, background). The instructions shown in the form explain the options.

Then create the handouts in Event > Handouts, choosing their model:

From the list you can download each handout as a PDF, ready to print.

Speed larp

Short scenes played before the event, to let participants get to know their characters. To use it, activate the Speed Larp feature.

Go to Event > Speed larp and click "New":

  • Name: name of the scene.
  • Text: the scene description.
  • Typ: the round of the scene: scenes of the same round are played at the same time.
  • Station: where the scene takes place.
  • Characters: the characters in the scene.

Participants see their scenes in their character page. If the Check option is enabled, Event > Check reports characters placed in two scenes of the same round, or missing from a round.

Workshops

Quiz-style questions that participants answer before the event, to check they know the rules or the setting. To use it, activate the Workshop feature.

Create the modules in Event > Modules, then their questions in Event > Questions and the possible answers, marking the correct ones, in Event > Answers:

Participants find a new entry, Workshop, in the event menu. Event > Workshops shows which participants have not yet completed all the modules in the last year.

Related tutorials: Plots, Characters, Event Tools

name: Event Tools
descr:
This tutorial covers smaller tools that help the staff before and during the event: tracking problems and milestones, hosting files, sharing protected media, and copying elements from another event.

Problems

A ticket system to log and follow issues during the event. To use it, activate the Problems feature.

Go to Event > Problems and click "New":

  • Severity: from 1 - RED (most serious) to 4 - GREEN.
  • Status: OPEN, WORKING or CLOSED.
  • Where: where the problem happened.
  • When: when it happened.
  • What: what happened.
  • Who: who is involved.

Staff members can add comments and take charge of a problem until it is closed.

Milestones

Track the preparation of the event with deadlines and owners. To use it, activate the Milestones feature.

Go to Event > Milestones and click "New":

  • Name: what must be done.
  • Status: To Do, In Progress or Completed.
  • Description: details.
  • Deadline: when it must be done.
  • Assigned to: the staff member responsible.

Hosting files

Upload files to LarpManager and share them with a link. To use it, activate the Utility feature.

Go to Event > Utility and click "New":

Each file gets a link, based on its Cod, that you can share with the staff or with participants. It is also useful to host the background images of PDF sheets and handouts.

One-time content

Stream a video or audio file through links that work only once. To use it, activate the One-Time Content feature.

Upload the file in Event > Content:

  • Content name: descriptive name of the content.
  • Description: optional description.
  • Media file: the video or audio file (MP4, WebM or MP3 recommended).
  • Active: uncheck to make the content unavailable.

Then generate the access links in Event > Tokens, with an optional note (for example the recipient). Each link can be opened only once; LarpManager records when it was used, by whom and from where.

Copying from another event

Reuse the setup of a previous event. To use it, activate the Copy feature.

Go to Event > Copy, choose the event to copy from in Parent, and select the elements to copy in Target (configuration, tickets, registration form, characters, factions, and more):

Note: elements of this event with the same name are overwritten.

Related tutorials: Writing Extras, Organization Tools, Check-in

name: Organization Tools
descr:
This tutorial covers organization-wide tools: shuttle requests, the warehouse, short links, the integration with an external app, and the activity log.

Shuttle

Let participants ask to be picked up, and organize the rides. To use it, activate the Shuttle feature.

Users find a new "Shuttle" page in their menu, where they submit a request:

  • Number of passengers: how many people need a ride.
  • Pickup location: the address or place of pickup.
  • Additional details: details to recognize them (clothes, luggage, meeting point).
  • Pickup date: the day of the ride.
  • Pickup time: the time of the ride.

The shuttle staff sees all requests in the same page and updates their status: "Waiting list", "We're coming", "Arrived safe and sound", adding instructions for the passengers (such as the car model).

Warehouse

Keep track of your props, costumes and equipment. To use it, activate the Warehouse feature.

Create the places where items are stored in Organization > Containers:

Then add the items in Organization > Items, each with its container, tags and photo:

Use Organization > Tags to group items, and Organization > Movements to record when items leave or return. For each event, Event > Area, Event > Items, Event > Checks and Event > Manifest let you plan which items go where, and check them before and after the event.

URL shortener

Create short links to long addresses. To use it, activate the URL shortener feature.

Go to Organization > URL shortener and click "New":

  • Name: a label for the link.
  • Cod: the short code of the link.
  • URL: the long address it redirects to.

App integration

Add a topbar button that sends logged-in users to your own application. To use it, activate the App Integration feature.

In Organization > Configuration > App Integration, set:

  • Button text: the label of the topbar button.
  • Redirect URL: the address of your application.
  • Shared secret: the key used to sign the login token, if your application supports single sign-on.
  • Algorithm: the signing algorithm of the token (default: HS256).

Activity log

See who created, changed or deleted what. To use it, activate the Activity Log feature.

The log of the whole organization is in Organization > Activity Log, and the log of each event in Event > Activity Log:

Related tutorials: Event Tools, Users

name: Italian Associations
descr:
This tutorial covers the features for associations based in Italy: fiscal receipts, the register of volunteers, the fiscal code check and the annual fiscal report.

Receipts

Generate a PDF fiscal receipt for each payment, as required by Italian law. To use it, activate the Receipt feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Receipts, set the data shown on the receipts:

  • Full name: the name of the association, as shown in the receipt header.
  • Legal address: the full address of the association.
  • Fiscal code: the tax code of the association.
  • RUNTS registration: the registration details, for example 'Iscritta al RUNTS sez. APS'.

Register of volunteers

Keep the register of volunteers required by the RUNTS regulations. To use it, activate the Register of volunteers feature.

Go to Organization > Volunteers to add volunteers and print the register:

Fiscal code check

Check the fiscal codes entered by your members. To use it, activate the Fiscal code check feature. Organization > Check data lists the members whose fiscal code does not match their personal data.

Annual fiscal report

An annual summary of your fiscal activity, for the Italian budget report. To use it, activate the Annual fiscal report feature, then open Organization > Balance.

Easter egg

Occasionally show users a special page, and optionally award them a badge. To use it, activate the Easter egg feature.

In Organization > Configuration > Easter egg, set:

  • Probability: how often the page is shown, out of a thousand page views.
  • Badge: the badge awarded to users who see it (see Badges in the Users tutorial).
  • Description: text shown on the special page.
  • Page: content of the special page.

Related tutorials: Accounting, Membership, Payments

name: Character References
descr:
Character references let you mention other characters in any text by their number instead of their name: names are always up to date, and participants can hover them to see who the character is. This tutorial explains the reference syntax, the tools to insert them, and how to check that they are consistent.

Enabling references

References need character numbers: enable Number in Event > Configuration > Character Sheet (see Character Sheet). Each character gets a number, starting from 1, shown next to its name in Event > Characters.

Writing a reference

In any text (character, plot, faction, and so on), write the number of a character after one of these symbols:

  • #XX: a mutual relationship, where the other character knows about it (love, colleagues, rivals);
  • @XX: a one-way relationship, where the other character does not know about it (secret hatred, unrequited love);
  • ^XX: only the name of the other character, with no relationship.

For example, this text written for character #2:

is shown to the participant with the current name of character #1, which they can hover to see the character and its participant:

Since the name is read when the text is shown, it stays correct even if the character is renamed later, or if a participant sets a custom name.

Character finder

While writing, type one of the symbols (#, @ or ^) to open a popup: type part of the character's name, and its number is inserted for you.

Select a reference number in the text to see the name of that character:

In Event > Configuration > Characters you can also set:

  • Disable character finder: turns off the popup, if the symbols get in the way of your writing;
  • Replacing names: character names written in full in a text are replaced by their reference automatically.

Checking references

Enable Check in Event > Configuration > Characters, then open Event > Check. It scans all texts and reports inconsistent references: for example, if character #2 refers to character #1 with #1 (a mutual relationship), but character #1 never mentions character #2.

The same page reports the other writing problems it finds, such as missing or extra relationships with factions.

Related tutorials: Characters, Character Sheet, Plots

name: PDF Generation
descr:
PDF generation turns character sheets, the character gallery and participant profiles into printable PDF files, with your own layout: page size, margins, header and footer, background, fonts and colors. This tutorial explains the options, and suggests how to obtain common effects.

Activating PDF generation

To use it, activate the PDF generation feature. The PDF of each character sheet is regenerated automatically whenever the character is updated.

To let participants download their own sheet from their character page, select PDF among the elements shown to participants in Event > Event.

Downloads and test generation

Go to Event > PDF:

At the top you can download:

  • Gallery Pdf: the portraits of all the characters (or Test gallery to preview it as a web page);
  • PDF Profiles: the profiles of all the participants;
  • Bulk download: a ZIP with the files you select (gallery, profiles, character sheets, faction sheets, handouts);
  • All printable sheets: a ZIP with the sheets of all the characters, ready to print.

Under "Try the sheet generation", select a character to generate its sheet:

  • Complete sheet: the full sheet, with your layout;
  • Lightweight sheet: a simpler version, formatted automatically for easy reading and printing.

The "(Test)" links show the sheet as a web page, which opens much faster than the PDF: use them while you adjust the layout.

Layout options

Below, the PDF options are saved as soon as you change them, so you can try the result right away.

  • Page size: A4, A5 or Letter, each also in landscape.
  • Page margin: empty space on each side of the page, in centimeters (for example 2 or 1.5).
  • Header: shows on top of each page the name of the organization, of the character and of the event.
  • Footer: shows on the bottom of each page the name of the event and the page number.
  • Background image: an image stretched over the whole page (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP).
  • Title font and Text font: font files (TTF or OTF) for the character name and titles, and for all the other text.
  • Title size and Text size: in percent of the standard size (100 = standard).
  • Title color, Text color, Link color, Highlight color (bold text) and Separator color (the lines under the header, over the footer and between sections).
  • CSS: your own style rules, applied after all the options above (see below).

Leave an option empty to keep the standard look. After changing the layout, click Regenerate (recreates all pdf: slow) at the bottom to rebuild all the existing PDFs (it can take a while).

For example, header, footer, a brown title color and a light separator color give this sheet:

Suggested effects

Most looks can be obtained with the options alone:

  • Parchment or letter look: upload a paper texture as Background image, a handwriting or calligraphy font as Title font, and a dark brown Title color. Keep the Page margin large enough (2-2.5 cm) so the text stays inside the paper edges of the image.
  • Themed sheet: use the colors of your event for Title color and Separator color, and the event font as Title font, keeping a plain, readable Text font.
  • Booklet (A5): choose A5 as Page size, a smaller margin (1-1.5 cm), and a Text size around 90; enable Footer for the page numbers.
  • Printer friendly: no background, black Text color, and a light Separator color, to save ink.

Tip: for the background, use an image with the same proportions as the page (about 1:1.41 for A4 and A5), at least 1240 pixels wide, so it is not distorted or blurred.

Custom CSS

For anything else, write your own rules in the CSS option. The main elements of the sheet are:

  • #char_name: the name of the character, at the top;
  • #char_present: the presentation and the fields under the name;
  • h1: the section titles (Plots, Factions, Relationships, and so on);
  • h2: the titles inside the texts;
  • .plot: the text of each plot;
  • #header_content and #footer_content: the header and the footer.

Some examples, to copy and adapt:

  • Underline the titles inside the texts: h2 { border-bottom: 1px solid #c9a36b; }
  • Start each section on a new page: h1 { page-break-before: always; }
  • Keep a title on the same page as the text that follows: h2 { -pdf-keep-with-next: true; }
  • Hide the presentation and fields: #char_present { display: none; }
  • Justify the text: p { text-align: justify; }

To use your own images or fonts only in some places, first upload them in Event > Utility (see Event Tools), then write their code between two #: it is replaced with the address of the file. For example, with a font uploaded with code quill:

@font-face { font-family: quill; src: url('#quill#'); } #char_name { font-family: quill; }

Rules written in the CSS option always win over the options above. To define the page yourself (size, margins, frames for header and footer), write your own @page rule: the options fill in only what your rule does not define. For example:

@page { size: A4; @frame content_frame { margin: 2cm; } }

Note: the PDF is produced with xhtml2pdf, which supports only part of CSS (no flexbox or grid, for example). For all the supported properties, see the xhtml2pdf documentation.

Related tutorials: Characters, Writing Extras, Event Tools
